title: Best Yoga Mats UK
short: Yoga mats compared by grip, thickness and portability, from budget studio mats to premium travel-friendly options.
intro: A yoga mat's grip and thickness matter more than price for how a class actually feels underfoot. This guide compares mats tested by Women's Running's team through real yoga classes, from budget studio staples to premium mats built for dynamic practice.

guide.a: Exercise mats are thicker and more foamy, protecting joints during explosive movements like squat jumps. Yoga mats are thinner, longer, and prioritise traction and grip over cushioning, better suited to full-body poses like Downward Dog. If you mainly do post-workout stretches, an exercise mat is fine; for a proper yoga class, a dedicated yoga mat works better.

guide.q: How thick should a yoga mat be?
guide.a: Most yoga mats run 4mm to 6mm thick. A thinner mat helps you feel more connected to the floor, useful for standing and arm balances, while a thicker mat suits anyone with sensitive knees or joints. Very thin mats (1-2mm) are designed as toppers for studio mats or for travel, not as a sole mat.

Very, especially for beginners or anyone who sweats during practice. A grippy mat prevents sliding during poses, which matters most for balance work. More advanced practitioners working on things like handstands sometimes prefer a less grippy surface, since they rely on finger grip rather than mat traction.

guide.q: Do I need alignment markings on my mat?
guide.a: Alignment lines, like those on the Liforme mat here, help with consistency in poses such as lunges and Warrior poses, which some practitioners find genuinely useful. Others find them distracting and prefer a plain mat to relax into their practice without visual cues.
